'''Desargorr''' was a [[Mountain/Legends|mountainous]] [[Planet/Legends|world]]<ref name="Xim" /> located in the [[Desargorr system/Legends|Desargorr system]].<ref name="TEA" /> It was a part of the [[Allied Tion sector/Legends|Allied Tion sector]] of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]],<ref name="Xim" /> situated within [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of<ref name="The Slice" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA" />

The surface of Desargorr, which had abundant deposits of [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]], was pitted by ruthless [[Mining/Legends|mining]] over the span of [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]]. For [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] ruler [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] at some point around [[25,100 BBY]], Desargorr was under the rule of [[Jaminere Marches]], a state centered on the world [[Jaminere/Legends|Jaminere]].<ref name="Xim" /> By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], the mountains of Desargorr were represented as a faded [[holograph]] at the booths of the [[Orman's Sky Palace]] [[Cantina/Legends|bar]] on the planet [[Lianna/Legends|Lianna]], one of the establishment's several such recreations of sights from the Allied Tion [[Sector/Legends|sector]] worlds.<ref name="Lianna">''[[Mission to Lianna]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Desargorr was introduced in ''[[Mission to Lianna]]'', a [[1992]] [[West End Games]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' adventure authored by [[Joanne E. Wyrick]].<ref name="Lianna" /> The [[December 7]], [[2009]] [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]<ref name="XimOriginal">{{SWArchive|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek01/index.html|text=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> article "[[Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster]]" by [[Jason Fry]] placed it in grid square S-6.<ref name="Xim" />
